guideTitle: The Best Reclining Office Chairs With Footrests for Breaks at Your Desk
metaTitle: Best Reclining Office Chairs With Footrests (2026)
metaDescription: We compared reclining office chairs on footrest design, headrest, lumbar support, seat width and weight capacity, and flag three popular chairs that do not include a footrest.
introParagraphs: A reclining chair with a footrest lets you lean back and put your feet up between tasks without leaving the desk. The two features are marketed together loosely, though: some chairs recline but have no footrest, and footrest length and sturdiness vary more than listings suggest.

Five chairs here include a pull-out or supplied footrest. Three do not; they are included as lower-cost or executive-style alternatives for buyers who decide a footrest is not essential, and each is clearly marked. Among the footrest chairs, the differences are weight capacity, headrest adjustment, lumbar design and seat shape.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, weight ratings and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $39 to $210 at the time of writing.

gtplayer-big-and-tall-400lbs-footrest.badge: Best Big and Tall With Footrest
gtplayer-big-and-tall-400lbs-footrest.summary: A 400 lb-rated high-back chair with a locking pull-out footrest and pocket-spring lumbar.
gtplayer-big-and-tall-400lbs-footrest.description:
The GTPLAYER Big and Tall is the footrest chair for larger users: it lists a 400 lb capacity, the highest here, on a wide high-back frame.

Its pull-out footrest locks when extended, and the lumbar cushion uses pocket springs rather than plain foam. GTPLAYER describes a 3D saddle-shaped seat and recline to a near-flat position.

It is bulky, so check the floor space behind and in front of the chair with the footrest out, and it costs about twice as much as the mid-priced footrest chairs.
cons: Costs about twice the mid-priced chairs
gtplayer-big-and-tall-400lbs-footrest.bestFor: Larger users who want a sturdy, locking footrest.
gtplayer-big-and-tall-400lbs-footrest.skipIf: You are of average build; the N-GEN or GTPLAYER swivel chair offers a footrest for less than half the price.

ngen-gaming-footrest-lumbar.summary: A high-back recliner with a pull-out footrest and height-adjustable lumbar for under $90.
ngen-gaming-footrest-lumbar.description:
The N-GEN is the value pick among the footrest chairs: a high-back recliner with a pull-out footrest and lumbar support that adjusts for height.

The high back supports the shoulders and head when reclined, which matters more on a footrest chair than on an upright task chair.

The armrests are fixed, the recline uses a tension mechanism rather than listed lock positions, and the leather-look cover runs warmer than mesh.
ngen-gaming-footrest-lumbar.bestFor: Buyers who want a footrest and high back at a moderate price.
ngen-gaming-footrest-lumbar.skipIf: You want an adjustable headrest; the GTPLAYER swivel chair lists one.

gtplayer-360-swivel-headrest-footrest.summary: A footrest chair with a separate adjustable headrest for support when reclined.
gtplayer-360-swivel-headrest-footrest.description:
This GTPLAYER model is the pick if head support while reclined matters: its headrest is a separate adjustable piece that can be raised to meet your head, rather than being molded into the backrest.

It keeps the pull-out footrest, 360-degree swivel and gas-lift height adjustment, at about half the price of the GTPLAYER Big and Tall.

The lumbar is a fixed cushion, the weight rating is lower than the Big and Tall's, and the recline uses a single tension setting.
cons: Lower capacity than the Big and Tall
gtplayer-360-swivel-headrest-footrest.bestFor: People who recline often and want the headrest at the right height.
gtplayer-360-swivel-headrest-footrest.skipIf: You want adjustable lumbar; the N-GEN lists it.

big-tall-flip-armrest-footrest.summary: A wide teddy-fleece seat, flip-up arms and a footrest for sitting cross-legged or reclining.
big-tall-flip-armrest-footrest.description:
This big and tall chair is for people who sit cross-legged or tuck a leg under: it has a wide teddy-fleece seat and flip-up armrests that get out of the way, plus an included footrest.

It has an executive-style high back and reclines. The fleece is softer than leatherette or mesh.

It is the most expensive chair here at the time of writing, fleece holds more heat, and the listing does not give a weight capacity despite the big and tall name. It has fewer buyer reviews than most chairs here.
big-tall-flip-armrest-footrest.bestFor: People who sit cross-legged and want a soft, wide seat with a footrest.
big-tall-flip-armrest-footrest.skipIf: You run warm; a mesh chair will be cooler, though none of the mesh chairs here have footrests.

homall-gaming-massage-lumbar-footrest.summary: A footrest chair with a vibrating massage lumbar cushion and adjustable headrest.
homall-gaming-massage-lumbar-footrest.description:
The Homall adds a vibrating massage lumbar cushion to the usual footrest-and-headrest layout, which none of the other chairs here include.

Otherwise it matches the mid-priced chairs: a pull-out footrest, adjustable headrest, reclining back and gas-lift swivel base, for about $85 at the time of writing.

The massage unit needs its own power, adds a little noise and is one more part that can fail. The listing does not give a weight capacity.
homall-gaming-massage-lumbar-footrest.bestFor: Buyers who want a massage cushion along with recline and a footrest.
homall-gaming-massage-lumbar-footrest.skipIf: You do not want the massage feature; the GTPLAYER swivel chair costs about the same.

neo-chair-mesh-task-no-footrest.summary: A low-cost mesh task chair with no footrest or listed recline range.
neo-chair-mesh-task-no-footrest.description:
The NEO CHAIR does not include a footrest, and its listing gives no recline range, so it does not meet the main brief of this guide. It is here as a budget alternative for buyers who decide a breathable task chair matters more.

It has a mid-back mesh seat and back, basic lumbar support and height adjustment, for under $40 at the time of writing.

If a footrest is the reason you are shopping, choose one of the chairs above.
neo-chair-mesh-task-no-footrest.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a breathable task chair and do not need a footrest.
neo-chair-mesh-task-no-footrest.skipIf: You want to recline with your feet up; this chair is not designed for that.

bestoffice-ergonomic-mesh-no-footrest.summary: A widely reviewed budget mid-back chair with no footrest or listed recline range.
bestoffice-ergonomic-mesh-no-footrest.description:
The BestOffice does not include a footrest or list a recline range. It is included as a widely reviewed budget alternative for buyers who decide a footrest is not essential.

It has a mid-back mesh backrest, basic lumbar support and height adjustment, for under $40 at the time of writing, and is the most widely reviewed chair here.

For reclining with your feet up, one of the footrest chairs above is the better fit.
bestoffice-ergonomic-mesh-no-footrest.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a basic task chair and do not need a footrest.
bestoffice-ergonomic-mesh-no-footrest.skipIf: A footrest is the reason you are shopping.

furmax-executive-leather-no-footrest.summary: A high-back PU leather executive chair with adjustable lumbar and recline, but no footrest.
furmax-executive-leather-no-footrest.description:
The Furmax executive chair reclines but does not include a footrest. It is here for buyers who prefer a traditional office look and are willing to add a separate footrest.

It has a high back, PU leather upholstery that wipes clean, and adjustable lumbar support, for about $90 at the time of writing.

PU leather runs warmer than mesh, and the listing does not describe recline lock positions.
furmax-executive-leather-no-footrest.bestFor: Buyers who want an executive look and will add a standalone footrest.
furmax-executive-leather-no-footrest.skipIf: You want an integrated footrest; the N-GEN costs about the same and includes one.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Recline does not imply a footrest. Five chairs here include one; the NEO CHAIR, BestOffice and Furmax do not.
A footrest that locks when extended, like the GTPLAYER Big and Tall's, should feel steadier. Listings rarely give footrest length, so check buyer feedback if you are tall.
A high back or adjustable headrest matters more on a reclining chair. The GTPLAYER swivel chair and Homall list adjustable headrests.
A fixed cushion set for upright sitting may sit in the wrong place when reclined. The N-GEN lists height-adjustable lumbar; the Homall a massage cushion.
Only the GTPLAYER Big and Tall states a capacity (400 lb). A reclined chair with the footrest out needs much more floor space than an upright one.

faq.q: Do all reclining office chairs have a footrest?
faq.a: No. Three chairs in this guide recline or sit upright without one. Check the listing for an explicit footrest rather than assuming.

faq.q: Will the footrest be long enough if I'm tall?
faq.a: Listings rarely give extension length. If you are tall, check buyer feedback for comments on calf support at full extension.

faq.q: Is a chair's weight limit the same reclined and upright?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If you are near a chair's limit, check whether the manufacturer gives a separate rating for reclined use.

faq.q: Why does lumbar support feel wrong when I recline?
faq.a: A fixed cushion is usually positioned for upright sitting and can end up in the wrong place as you lean back. Adjustable lumbar lets you reposition it.

faq.q: Should I buy a chair without a footrest if I mainly sit upright?
faq.a: That can be a sensible choice. The NEO CHAIR, BestOffice and Furmax cover upright work, and a standalone footrest can be added later.

faq.q: How much space does a reclining chair need?
faq.a: Considerably more than upright, once the backrest is reclined and the footrest extended. Measure the space behind and in front of the chair before buying one of the larger models.

bottomLine: Among the footrest chairs, the N-GEN is the value choice with adjustable lumbar, the GTPLAYER swivel chair suits anyone who wants an adjustable headrest, and the Homall adds a massage cushion. The GTPLAYER Big and Tall is worth paying more for with a larger build, and the flip-arm chair suits people who sit cross-legged.

If you decide a footrest is not essential, the NEO CHAIR and BestOffice are inexpensive upright chairs and the Furmax offers an executive look, but none of the three is designed for reclining with your feet up.
